questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Building Localized Applications”?
options: Building Localized Applications should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Building Localized Applications helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Building Localized Applications means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Building Localized Applications removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Building Localized Applications helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Building Localized Applications is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

options: Connect “Configuring the source locale” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Configuring the source locale” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Configuring the source locale” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.

questions.answer_key: Connect “Configuring the source locale” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Configuring the source locale” under Building Localized Applications. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Building Localized Applications”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
